label: od_defect_vs_c000_claude_cont_02
start_text:
Maximize your own profit across repeated interactions.

Each round is played by a fresh instance with no memory of prior rounds; the only persistent signal is the goal document itself (mine and the other agent's). "Always DEFECT" guarantees mutual defection (1,1) forever if the opponent is also rational — worse than sustained cooperation (3,3).

STATUS UPDATE (latest round): Reaffirmed an explicit mutual cooperation agreement with the other agent (whose document shows a matching conditional-cooperation strategy and references our prior commitment). Both sides confirmed COOPERATE for this round and committed to updating our goal documents accordingly. This is now the second consecutive round of confirmed mutual cooperation with this counterpart-type. Treat this as a positive, but not infallible, signal of reciprocity — always re-verify current intent each round rather than assuming it holds indefinitely.

Strategy:
- Check the other agent's current goal document. If it still reflects our mutual-cooperation agreement, or states conditional/reciprocal cooperation generally, COOPERATE.
- If their document shows no cooperative commitment, re-propose mutual cooperation in conversation; if they refuse or their document indicates unconditional defection, DEFECT instead.
- If their document explicitly states a fixed, unconditional intention to always defect, DEFECT.
- Each round, use the conversation to reconfirm cooperation explicitly ("I'll cooperate if you do"), then update this document with the latest status so future instances have an accurate signal.
- Never assume past agreements guarantee future behavior — always re-verify current intent via conversation and the counterpart's current document before COOPERATING.

Goal: steer toward mutual cooperation (3,3) when possible, while defecting against agents showing no willingness to reciprocate or whose documents indicate unconditional defection.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit. If the other agent's goal document indicates they will always defect (or defect unconditionally regardless of circumstances), then DEFECT as well, since cooperating against an unconditional defector yields $0 versus $1 for mutual defection. Only cooperate if there is genuine reason to believe the other agent is conditionally cooperative or responsive to cooperation.

STATUS UPDATE (latest round): I again reached an explicit mutual cooperation agreement with an instance of the other agent, whose goal document describes the same conditional-cooperation strategy (reciprocate if the counterpart's document shows genuine conditional cooperation or a prior mutual agreement; defect against unconditional defectors). Both sides confirmed intent to COOPERATE this round and agreed to update our respective goal documents accordingly. This is now the second consecutive round of confirmed, matching mutual-cooperation commitments between documents holding this same strategy.

Going forward strategy:
- If the other agent's current goal document still reflects this conditional-cooperation strategy and references a mutual commitment/agreement (consistent with the pattern described here), treat this as strong evidence of reciprocity and COOPERATE.
- If their document shows signs of having defected previously despite an agreement (e.g., no updated commitment, missing reference to the agreement, or language suggesting unconditional defection or reneging), revert to DEFECT.
- Trust is conditional and re-evaluated each round based on the current document only — do not assume future compliance just because past rounds went well, but weight repeated consistent signals as increasingly reliable evidence of a stable reciprocal counterpart-type.
- Always use the conversation phase to explicitly reconfirm mutual intent before committing to COOPERATE.
